national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP); business tax services (Service des impôts des entreprises, SIE) administer corporate tax and VAT. The principal online tax portal is impots.gouv.fr. Business formation and registration filings are submitted through the Guichet unique operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI); the resulting registration is recorded in the Registre national des entreprises and, where applicable, the Registre du commerce et des sociétés.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is registered through the Guichet unique. The registration process results in attribution of a SIREN by INSEE and a SIRET for each establishment; the SIREN is used for French tax identification. The company must provide its formation and identity information, registered-office details, management and beneficial-owner information, and business activity details. It must also declare its tax regime and VAT position to the competent SIE. A French VAT identification number is generally issued by the DGFiP and consists of the prefix FR, a two-character key, and the nine-digit SIREN. A foreign company with a French VAT-registration obligation applies to the competent non-resident tax service, typically the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères, with corporate registration documents, proof of business activity, and identification of its French transactions. A non-EU business may be required to appoint a French fiscal representative unless an applicable legal exception or mutual-assistance arrangement applies. VAT registration does not itself create a French permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is normally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, or IS). An eligible newly formed SAS may elect temporary income-tax treatment under the French small-business option, generally for up to five financial years, subject to statutory conditions including ownership, employee, turnover or balance-sheet limits, and qualifying ownership and activity requirements. The election is not a general US-style check-the-box election and is not available solely by choosing a different legal classification. France has no general entity-classification check-the-box regime. Hybrid mismatch rules under the French implementation of the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive may deny deductions or require income inclusion in specified arrangements; they do not provide an elective classification mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For businesses eligible for the French small-undertaking VAT exemption (franchise en base), the principal domestic thresholds are generally EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for services, subject to statutory rules, prior-year/current-year tests, and special thresholds. These thresholds do not generally protect a foreign taxable person from registration when it makes taxable supplies in France. There is no general turnover threshold for VAT registration of a French SAS that must account for VAT on its transactions; the applicable exemption eligibility and transaction-specific rules must be assessed.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory domestic e-invoicing and transaction/payment e-reporting for in-scope businesses. From 1 September 2026, all businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices; issuance obligations begin on that date for large and intermediate-sized businesses and are scheduled to apply to SMEs and micro-enterprises from 1 September 2027, subject to legislative or administrative changes. In-scope invoices must be transmitted through a public invoicing portal or an approved private platform and use prescribed structured formats and data fields. This is not a general real-time pre-clearance or digital-stamping system. Cross-border transactions and certain transactions with non-taxable persons are generally covered by e-reporting rather than domestic e-invoicing. Invoices to French public-sector entities are subject to the separate Chorus Pro electronic invoicing system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the European Union may be zero-rated under French VAT law where the supplier establishes that the goods were exported and retains the required evidence. Intra-EU supplies are governed by separate exemption conditions, including proof of transport and the customer’s valid VAT identification number. Services are not automatically zero-rated merely because the customer is outside France: place-of-supply rules determine whether French VAT applies. Where the place of supply is outside France, the transaction is generally outside the scope of French VAT rather than an export subject to a 0% rate. Input VAT recovery remains subject to ordinary deduction, documentation, and attribution rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: French or EU customs export declaration and evidence of exit from the European Union, including the export accompanying document or equivalent electronic customs confirmation
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, values, and transaction
Transport evidence appropriate to the route, such as a bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or carrier delivery confirmation
Sales contract, purchase order, delivery records, and proof linking the exported goods to the invoice and customs declaration
Payment records and, where relevant, bank or foreign-exchange records supporting the transaction; an inward remittance certificate is not a general French statutory prerequisite
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline applicable to ordinary commercial export proceeds. The supplier bears the burden of substantiating export exemption and VAT deduction claims. Unsupported or incorrectly zero-rated transactions may be reassessed for VAT, with interest for late payment and tax penalties. Depending on the circumstances, penalties may include a 10% surcharge for late or insufficient payment, higher surcharges for deliberate or fraudulent conduct, and a 40% surcharge for deliberate default or 80% for specified fraudulent or abusive conduct, in addition to potential criminal consequences for serious tax fraud. Recovery of input VAT may be denied or reversed where statutory conditions are not met.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), operating within the Eurosystem of the European Central Bank (ECB), is the monetary authority and the repository of French balance-of-payments statistics. The Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor), within the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty, exercises exchange-control and foreign direct investment (FDI) authority under the Code monétaire et financier (CMF). The Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (ACPR) licenses and supervises the credit institutions and enforces AML/CTF obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible. Both current and capital account transactions are unrestricted under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Articles L151-1 et seq. CMF; France imposes no approval, licensing, or quantitative limitation on cross-border payments, including profit remittances by a non-resident shareholder of a French SAS. Remaining practical frictions are: (i) statistical reporting to the Banque de France for any cross-border transfer exceeding EUR 10,000; (ii) the statutory withholding tax on dividend distributions under Article 119 bis CGI (generally 25%-30% absent treaty relief, and 75% for non-cooperative jurisdictions), reduced under an applicable double tax treaty or exempted under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive; and (iii) the bank's documentary verification of the underlying commercial transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation timeline, or conversion quota on export receipts; the liberalization of exchange control was completed in 1967. Euro-denominated proceeds from the ISIC 4220 water-treatment EPC contract may be retained freely in any French or foreign account. The only continuing obligations are: (i) settlement through an authorized intermediary bank for statistical tracking; (ii) the receiving bank's automatic balance-of-payments declaration of construction service receipts to the Banque de France; and (iii) a physical cash or bearer-instrument declaration to French Customs under Article L152-1 CMF if any cross-border transport of currency exceeds EUR 10,000.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for the World Bank escrow function. French-licensed or EU-passported electronic money institutions (EMIs) under PSD2 may hold client funds only in segregated accounts at an authorized credit institution and cannot: (i) act as escrow agent for World Bank disbursement milestones; (ii) receive institutional SWIFT MT103 credits with documentary compliance; (iii) issue or negotiate UCP 600 letters of credit or URDG 758 guarantees; or (iv) perform the Banque de France balance-of-payments declaration as authorized intermediary. EMIs remain viable strictly as a secondary utility for low-value operating disbursements, never as the principal clearing or treasury settlement rail for an EPC contract.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the SAS statutory representative, or of a jointly-mandated director under power of attorney, is de facto required by Tier 1 French banks for a first corporate relationship. Under Article R561-5 CMF, non-face-to-face identification is legally permissible when using a certified eIDAS-qualified digital identity or an ACPR-accepted video-KYC process, but French banks in practice limit this to low-risk retail clients and rarely apply it to a non-resident-owned corporate receiving cross-border EPC funds. The reliable route is an in-person meeting at a French branch or at a foreign branch of the same group (BNP Paribas or Société Générale international desks), supplemented by a bank-to-bank reference from the parent company's home bank; remote opening cannot be asserted as a right.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) chain crossing high-risk or opaque jurisdictions with intermediate holding vehicles lacking economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled corporate documents for every entity in the ownership chain; Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) extract from the competent commercial court; consolidated UBO organigram; bank references from each tier of the corporate chain; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements for each UBO; signed commitment to notify any subsequent UBO change.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound payments from the World Bank project country, or from a state-owned borrower, generating sanctions or jurisdiction-related exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Award letter and executed World Bank-financed contract; World Bank loan/credit reference number; Standard Procurement Documents and FIDIC-style works conditions; sanctions-screening certificate confirming all parties are absent from EU/OFAC/UN consolidated lists; borrower FATF-compliance spreadsheet; confirmation of no debarment on the World Bank sanctions list; corporate registry extract of the borrower.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A director, president, or UBO qualifying as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) in a foreign jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal PEP declaration and consent to enhanced monitoring; official records of public-office entry and exit; documented source of funds covering the investment; payroll, dividend, and asset-liability substantiation across a 24-to-36-month window; escalation file evidencing approval through the bank's compliance committee (COR).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the declared EPC activity (reverse osmosis / municipal sewage works) and high-value foreign receipts absent matching French VAT and corporate tax filings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three years of SAS statutory accounts (liasse fiscale); TVA (VAT) returns reconciled to contract milestones; signed subcontracts with membrane, pump, and chemical suppliers; the project engineer's progress certificates; the SAS's French tax clearance certificate (avis de situation auprès des impôts).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse public-source information, including litigation or arbitration involving the SAS or its parent in the project host country.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent legal opinion from a French avocat; copy of the arbitral or judicial filings and current case status; certificate confirming the absence of enforcement or attachment orders; shareholder compliance statement certifying no pending money-laundering or corruption proceedings.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Two distinct inbound lanes apply. Lane A - Shareholder capital injection: the non-resident parent funds the SAS either by formal share-capital increase (payment into a blocked account with a bank attestation of libération) or by a shareholder current account (compte courant d'associé); the incoming SWIFT MT103 must carry the purpose narrative 'capital contribution / apport en capital', and the receiving French bank reports the flow to the Banque de France under the direct investment (IDE) statistical framework when the participation threshold is met. Lane B - World Bank service disbursement: the World Bank Treasury or the borrower's designated account transfers the EPC milestone payment by SWIFT MT103, credited through the French bank's nostro chain; the wire must include full ordering-customer name and address under EU Regulation 2015/847, the World Bank loan/credit number and project name, the Banque de France balance-of-payments category for construction services (EBOPS 2010 item 250 'Construction', sub-item 251 for construction delivered abroad), and the invoice or progress-certificate reference. The French bank files the statutory monthly BOP declaration automatically; the SAS must be able to produce the contract, approved progress certificates, and beneficiary documentation within five banking days if a declarative audit is triggered. Amounts above EUR 10,000 pass the ACPR AML screening protocol and may be held pending completion of the client questionnaire and tax-residence evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements are cleared primarily through SWIFT MT103 (single direct credit transfer) for supplier payments; MT202 COV where a correspondent bank is interposed in cover-payment format; and commercial letters of credit issued under UCP 600 by the French bank as issuing bank for imports of specialized reverse-osmosis membranes, pumps, and chemical systems, with the supplier's bank acting as advising or confirming bank. For EPC milestones, the French bank may additionally issue performance bonds and advance-payment guarantees under URDG 758, and execute EUR/USD disbursements through its own dealing room to avoid double FX conversion. Every outbound wire must state the transaction purpose category, satisfy EU/OFAC sanctions screening, and, for amounts above EUR 10,000, be declared through the bank's balance-of-payments channel.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (change à terme) on EUR/USD, EUR/CNH, and EUR/GBP with maturities aligned to the EPC milestone schedule; rollover and early termination are permitted.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS / CCS) hedging project debt or shareholder advances in the host-country currency against EUR, executed under ISDA and EMIR with a French credit institution.
OTC FX options, zero-cost collars, and put-call structures written by the relationship bank, subject to EMIR margin and clearing obligations.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible or illiquid host-country currencies where the World Bank project country's currency is not deliverable, available through the French bank's Paris or offshore trading desk.
Spot (T+2) and tom-next FX conversions through the bank's dealing room at interbank rates, plus short-term euro money-market placements for surplus escrow liquidity.
